criteria.name: artwork_craft
criteria.why: The register meets the bold test. Preflight measures median L* 4.5, 13.3 and 2.7 on frames 1, 5 and 9. Frame 5's nine lamps with one lit cyan head, frame 7's map slab and frame 9's lit run of day lamps into dark bluestem are strong. The hero model reads as a primitive on several frames. On frame 4 the wing is a thin slab floating above the cabin roof, its strut runs diagonally through the cabin windows, the spinner has no propeller or disc, and the belly pod hovers. The strut also crosses the windows on frame 1 (about x 1150 to 1600, y 1000 to 1340) and on the left plane of frame 3. On frame 3 the bottom 45 percent is bare concrete (about y 1300 to 1960 of 2000) and both airframes are cut off in the top band. On frame 2 the tower base is a flat L-shaped slab that reads as a placeholder, and the tail-on Caravan reads as a tangle of strut and propeller across the fuselage. Several frames lean on a primitive model, below the 7 descriptor.

criteria.name: deck_coherence
criteria.why: It reads as one deck: one Caravan in one white and navy material, one night apron, one cyan accent and one west key. The thread leaves frame 1 by the right edge and enters frame 2 from the left to land on the tower cab. The storyboard declares MOTIF_EVOLUTION, CAMERA_MOVE and EDGE_TEASE, and they show in the strip. Frame 7, the map, is the one frame outside the hero, and only the city lamp heads tie it back. Frame 5's brown haze band (y 250 to 850) is warmer than the navy-black sky on the other frames.

criteria.name: claim_integrity
criteria.why: Every numeral on the slides and in the caption traces. 28 and 1,096 come from compute.py (Sept 10 2026 to Sept 10 2029 is 1,096 days, which I checked). 8, 26, more than 30 and sixth come from the c3, c5, c6 and c7 quotes, which I checked against faa_launch.txt. 'Neither TxDOT's release nor the FAA's names Merlin' holds, because neither snapshot contains 'Merlin'. The c28 stretch is repaired: the claim text and the web edition now say what the quote says, attributed to Merlin. Three faults keep this under 7. (1) No slide or caption sentence uses c33, the Dallas Innovates caption credited to TxDOT showing 'A modified Cessna 208B Grand Caravan operated by Merlin Labs participates in the Project Nexus test flights'. TxDOT's release links 'View photos and video from the event', and nobody fetched that gallery. So 'TxDOT's and the FAA's releases skip Merlin' in the caption, and 'The state's and the FAA's accounts of the day do not name it' in the web edition dek, leave a reader thinking there is no state trace of Merlin when the run holds one. Frame 3 cites c33 without saying what it shows. (2) Merlin's release is cited through Finviz's syndication although a GlobeNewswire original exists. (3) The caption's 'Medical and cargo logistics come next' rests on c17, which the first comment's TxDOT line omits.

criteria.name: story_and_stakes
criteria.why: A Texan learns what happened (Project Nexus phase one kicked off), where (Fort Worth Alliance Airport), who decided (TxDOT, with the FAA's March selection) and what comes next (medical and cargo, then passengers). The stake, whether software worked the radio with or without a pilot aboard, stays abstract. The deck gives no county, no body a reader can reach, no comment window and nothing to do.

criteria.name: sequence_and_momentum
criteria.why: The cover question earns the swipe and frame 2 pays with place and launch. The turn is frame 5's lamp table, one yes in nine cells. Frames 6 and 8 are program context that could move or merge without loss. Frame 9's closing line repeats frame 5's pilot-aboard absence.

criteria.name: voice
criteria.why: Clean and carefully attributed ('Merlin says', 'by two companies' word'). The house rules hold: no colons, no dashes, no banned words, no year in the post. Lines like 'The flights collect data and validate routes.' (frame 6) and 'It will use the data to write new rules.' (frame 8) are flat, and Alliance, Perot Field and the Metroplex get no local texture.

criteria.name: variety
criteria.why: The subject is new (tx-2026-0205), and the lamp table and the day-lamp runway are fresh. It is the third autonomous-vehicle deck in six days, after Kodiak on October 3rd and Saronic on October 7th. Each carries one illustrative vehicle through the deck, and Kodiak's also turned on who is aboard ('The observer is never placed aboard'), so the opening move and the central absence repeat.

one_sentence_fix: Add one sentence on frame 3 or 5 saying that a TxDOT-credited photo (c33, via Dallas Innovates) shows Merlin's Caravan in the Project Nexus test flights, and fetch TxDOT's linked event gallery, so that 'TxDOT's and the FAA's releases skip Merlin' stops implying the state left no trace of Merlin.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: This broadside elevation is the diagram frame, and the airframe reads as a primitive. The wing is a flat slab floating above the cabin roof, the strut passes through the cabin windows, the spinner has no blades or disc, and the belly pod hovers.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Seat the wing on a modelled roof fairing, end the strut at a lower-fuselage fitting below the windows, and fit frame 6's twisted three-blade propeller to the spinner.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: About 45 percent of the frame is bare concrete (y 1300 to 1960 of 2000). Both Caravans are cut off in the top band, Joby's nose off the left and Merlin's showing only its nose, and the left plane's strut crosses its windows.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Lower the camera aim about 12 degrees so both airframes sit whole in the middle band, crop the empty apron, and re-route the strut to its fuselage fitting.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The tower base is a flat L-shaped slab that reads as a placeholder. The tail-on Caravan reads as a tangle, with a strut across the fuselage and the propeller poking out beside it.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Model the tower base as a lit two-storey block on the ground with a contact shadow, and yaw the Caravan about 30 degrees so the fin and stabiliser silhouette reads clear of the struts.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: On the cover, the wing strut runs straight through the cabin windows (x 1150 to 1600, y 1000 to 1340), and the gear and concrete read clean.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: End the strut at a lower-fuselage fitting below the windows, and add grime and oil to the gear pants and the concrete around the nose wheel.
